results.name: Demo 1: general question answered with sources and contacts
results.detail:
How to apply for the homestead exemption

The homestead exemption takes $7,500 off your assessed value, which equals the first $75,000 of market value. It applies only to the home you own and live in as your primary residence, and you must own and occupy it by December 31 of the tax year [S2][S3][S7].

How to apply: All owners who live in the home must go in person to the Assessor's Office, City Hall, 1300 Perdido St., Room 4E01 [S8][S9]. Bring:

Proof of ownership: act of sale or deed
A Louisiana driver's license or state ID showing the property address
A current Entergy (or cable) bill for the property. The name, service address, and mailing address must match [S7][S8].

If your mailing address differs from the property, you'll need a recorded power of attorney. A married couple gets only one homestead [S9].

In Orleans the exemption reduces state, general city, school, levee, and levee-district taxes [S2], but not every millage.

SOURCES
S2 La. Const. Art. VII §20 (homestead exemption)
S3 La. R.S. 47:1703 (homestead statute)

results.name: '2027 reassessment' is a question, not an address
results.detail:
What the 2027 reassessment is

Louisiana reappraises every property at least every four years [S1]. The last reappraisal set values at the market as of Jan. 1, 2023, and those values are used for tax years 2024 through 2027 [S32]. That's why the 2027 roll the Assessor filed on Sept. 4, 2026 keeps 98% of values the same as 2026 [S31].

So the 2027 reassessment is the next reappraisal, done during 2027. It should set new values for the 2028 roll, posted for inspection in summer 2027, with bills due in early 2028. I'm inferring that timing from the four-year cycle [S32][S1], so please confirm it with the Assessor's Office. The last reappraisal raised total assessed value about 20% [S26].

Orleans names each roll for the year the bill is due. The "2027 roll" was posted in July–August 2026 [S4] and its bills come in early 2027.

What it means for owners: (1) your value may change in 2027 even if you change nothing; (2) when total values rise, taxing bodies must roll back millage, so your bill doesn't rise by the same percent, though they can vote to roll forward [S11]; (3) the summer 2027 open-roll period is the time to check your new value and appeal if you disagree; (4) make sure your homestead or freeze is on file before then. Status: the appeal window for the 2027 roll closed at 4 p.m. on Thursday, Aug. 20, 2026 [S4]. The next window, for the 2028 roll, should open in summer 2027 (it usually runs mid-July to mid-August) [S4][S5]. The exact dates haven't been announced, so I don't know them yet.

SOURCES
S1 La. Const. Art. VII §18 (classification, ratios, reappraisal)

results.name: Installments: sourced answer (no formal plan, partial payments)
results.detail:
Payment plans and partial payments

The City doesn't offer a formal installment plan for property taxes. You can make partial payments in person or by mail, but not online. Any unpaid balance is charged interest at 1% per month, plus other fees [S34].

For help with a bill you can't pay, contact the Bureau of the Treasury [S27]. If the problem is the value itself, that's a question for the Assessor's Office, and an appeal is only possible during the summer appeal window.

Property tax amendments on the November 2026 ballot: results

On Nov. 3, 2026, Louisiana voters decided several property tax amendments [S36][S20]:

Amendment 1, approved (about 75%): a disabled veteran's surviving spouse can move the exemption to a new home once.
Amendment 6, approved (about 65%): parishes and cities may choose to give owners 65 and older extra relief, with local approval. It does nothing in New Orleans unless the City adopts it, and I don't know of any such step.
Amendment 9, approved (about 60%): raises the Special Assessment Level ("freeze") income limit to below $150,000.
Amendment 2, rejected: would have let local governments keep lower millages after a reassessment without losing the right to raise them later.
Amendment 10, rejected: a local-option exemption for rehabilitated blighted property.

These are unofficial election-night results; confirm the certified results with the Secretary of State. I don't know exactly when each change takes effect, so ask the Assessor's Office. I don't take positions on ballot measures.

SOURCES
S36 WAFB / Fox 8 — Louisiana voters pass 7 of 10 constitutional amendments (Nov. 3, 2026; unofficial results) secondary
S20 PAR Louisiana — Guide to the Fall 2026 Constitutional Amendments secondary

results.detail:
How to apply for the homestead exemption

The homestead exemption takes $7,500 off your assessed value, which equals the first $75,000 of market value. It applies only to the home you own and live in as your primary residence, and you must own and occupy it by December 31 of the tax year [S2][S3][S7].

How to apply: All owners who live in the home must go in person to the Assessor's Office, City Hall, 1300 Perdido St., Room 4E01 [S8][S9]. Bring:

Proof of ownership: act of sale or deed
A Louisiana driver's license or state ID showing the property address
A current Entergy (or cable) bill for the property. The name, service address, and mailing address must match [S7][S8].

If your mailing address differs from the property, you'll need a recorded power of attorney. A married couple gets only one homestead [S9].

In Orleans the exemption reduces state, general city, school, levee, and levee-district taxes [S2], but not every millage.

SOURCES
S2 La. Const. Art. VII §20 (homestead exemption)
S3 La. R.S. 47:1703 (homestead statute)

RECORDED IN THE 2026 AND 2027 ROLLS

Computed tax on the 2027 roll (your next bill, due early 2027): $1,030 at 133.48 mills, after a homestead reduction of $915 [S31].

Computed tax on the 2026 roll (bills that were due early 2026): $1,019, from 131.99 total mills, after a homestead reduction of $904. Taxable assessed value: $7,070 [S30].

The 2027 file was filed Sept. 4, 2026, before the City Council approved a partial roll-forward of 4.039 mills on Nov. 5, 2026 [S33]. If those mills are added on top, this bill would rise by about $29 to $59 a year (4.039 × $7,070 taxable to × $14,570 assessed, depending on how much homestead reduces them ÷ 1,000). CALCULATED BY THE NAVIGATOR

Check: $14,570 assessed × 131.99 mills ÷ 1,000 = $1,923, − $904 homestead reduction = $1,019. Matches the recorded amount.

WHAT IT MEANS

Homestead reduces every levy except the police and fire millages "without homestead exemption" (11.51 mills), so you still pay those on the first $7,500 [S30]. results.name: AI answer with an invented number is rejected; checked answer shown
results.detail:
How your property tax bill is calculated (worked example)

Tax = (assessed value − exemptions) × millage ÷ 1,000, added up across every millage that applies to the property [S11][S17].

Step	Math	Result
Fair market value	set by Assessor	$300,000
× 10% residential ratio	$300,000 × 0.10	$30,000 assessed
− Homestead exemption	$30,000 − $7,500	$22,500 taxable
× 131.99 mills (2026 roll, East Bank)	$22,500 × 0.13199	$2,969.78
+ police & fire mills homestead doesn't reduce	$7,500 × 0.01151	$86.33
Total		$3,056.10 / year
Same home, no homestead	$30,000 × 0.13199	$3,959.70 / year

Sources: ratio [S1], homestead amount [S2], millage rates and the police/fire exception from the 2026 roll's millage file [S30].

Caveats: 131.99 is the total on the East Bank; Algiers (District 5) is 132.01 because it's in a different levee district [S30]. Special districts like the Downtown Development District or a neighborhood security district add fees that aren't in this total [S17]. Find your property above to see its own recorded tax.

SOURCES
S11 City of New Orleans Treasury — Millages: How Taxes are Calculated
S17 Bureau of Governmental Research — About Your Property Taxes secondary
S1 La. Const. Art. VII §18 (classification, ratios, reappraisal)
S2 La. Const. Art. VII §20 (homestead exemption)
S30 Louisiana Tax Commission — Orleans 2026 tax roll files, incl. millage by parcel (posted Nov. 2025)

What a mill (millage rate) is

A mill is one-tenth of one percent: $1 of tax per $1,000 of taxable assessed value [S13][S11].

Each taxing body (the City, School Board, levee and drainage districts, libraries, police, fire, and others) sets its own millage, and some changes need voter approval. They add up to your total rate [S11]. BGR reports which rates apply where [S18]. In the 2026 roll the total is 131.99 mills on the East Bank and 132.01 in Algiers; the 2027 roll raises the East Bank total to 133.48 [S30][S31].

You can't appeal a millage. Rates change through public hearings and elections [S13].

SOURCES

S11 City of New Orleans Treasury — Millages: How Taxes are Calculated
